analysis.step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core architecture components from the visual diagram and audio transcript for MakeMyTrip's Next-Gen SOC.
2. Ingestion layer receives events from public cloud ('AWS', represented by VPC icon) and on-premises systems ('ON-PREM', represented by ThirdParty icon) into the real-time stream processing engine ('APACHE METRON', hosted on EC2).
3. Metron streams persistent data into the Security Data Lake, where Amazon EMR transforms data into Amazon S3 storage, and Amazon Athena performs SQL queries and long-term profiling, feeding insights back into Apache Metron.
4. Metron triggers alerts to the SOAR framework ('SOAR', hosted on EC2), which notifies SOC analysts ('ALERTS', mapped to UserCompanyAnalyst), who can then execute automated mitigation via AWS WAF ('WAF').

graph.name: MakeMyTrip Next-Gen Security Operations Center (SOC) Architecture
graph.categories: security, data lake, stream processing, incident response
graph.notes: MakeMyTrip's next-gen SOC handles ~5000 events/sec across cloud and on-premises environments. It parses and enriches logs using Apache Metron, stores long-term telemetry in an S3/Athena security data lake, and automates threat response using SOAR and AWS WAF.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core services from the visual diagram and transcript: Amazon Macie, Amazon S3, Amazon Athena, Amazon QuickSight, AWS Glue, and a MySQL data lake (mapped to ThirdParty).
2. Pruned the 'Security Engineers' actor as per Rule 5 (human actors removed unless serving as direct API entry points).
3. Retained member account Macie and S3 instances representing production accounts being monitored.
4. Established logical data flows: Macie outputs findings metadata to the main account S3 bucket; Athena queries findings from S3; QuickSight visualizes query results from Athena; S3 metadata is exported/loaded into MySQL.

graph.name: Opportune Sensitive Data Discovery and Security Posture Management with Amazon Macie
graph.notes: Architecture for automated sensitive PII discovery (SSNs, ITINs, government IDs) across production AWS accounts using Amazon Macie with 95% detection accuracy. Metadata findings are stored in S3, queried via Athena, aggregated via Glue into MySQL, and presented in QuickSight dashboards for security remediation.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Inventory Icons: Identified 11 icons on the architecture board: ON-PREM (ThirdParty), MIGRATION TEAM (UserCompanyAgent), SLACK (ThirdParty), APP DISCOVERY SERVICE (AppDiscovery), DYNAMODB (DynamoDB), EC2 Migration Factory (EC2), CLOUDENDURE (ThirdParty), EC2 HOT REPLICA (EC2), BAKE AMI (AMI), SHARED AMI (AMI), and EC2 TARGET (EC2).
2. Vocabulary Normalization: Mapped third-party components (Slack, CloudEndure, On-Prem) to 'ThirdParty'. Mapped human migration actor to 'UserCompanyAgent'. Mapped AWS native services to their exact schema names ('AppDiscovery', 'DynamoDB', 'EC2', 'AMI').
3. Edge & Flow Construction:
   - Flow 0 (Continuous Replication & Pre-Migration Discovery): On-Prem sends metadata to App Discovery Service and streams block data to EC2 Hot Replica controlled by CloudEndure. Migration team populates target configurations into DynamoDB.
   - Flow 1 (Orchestrated Migration Execution): Migration team triggers Slack command -> Slack calls Migration Factory EC2 API -> EC2 queries DynamoDB & App Discovery Service -> EC2 stops CloudEndure replication -> EC2 bakes AMI -> AMI is shared to target account -> EC2 launches target EC2 instance with metadata configuration.

graph.name: AWS Migration Factory Automation Architecture
graph.notes: An automated migration factory architecture using AWS Application Discovery Service, CloudEndure, and EC2 to drastically reduce migration times from hours to 10 minutes.

nodes.name: ON-PREM
nodes.notes: Source on-premises environment containing workloads and data to be migrated.

nodes.name: MIGRATION TEAM
nodes.notes: Operations and migration engineering team managing the migration process and target parameters.

nodes.name: SLACK
nodes.notes: ChatOps platform used to trigger single-command automated migration workflows.

nodes.name: APP DISCOVERY SERVICE
nodes.notes: AWS Application Discovery Service collecting network connections and server utilization metrics.

nodes.name: DYNAMODB
nodes.notes: DynamoDB table storing target account metadata, subnet IDs, static IPs, and tags.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Migration Factory EC2 instance orchestrating discovery querying, AMI creation, and target provisioning.

nodes.name: CLOUDENDURE
nodes.notes: CloudEndure service managing continuous block-level volume replication.

nodes.name: EC2 HOT REPLICA
nodes.notes: Staging EC2 instance receiving continuous block-level replication from on-premises.

nodes.name: BAKE AMI
nodes.notes: Amazon Machine Image created from the continuous replication staging volume.

nodes.name: SHARED AMI
nodes.notes: Encrypted AMI shared across account boundaries into the target AWS account.

nodes.name: EC2 TARGET
nodes.notes: Final EC2 instance launched in the destination account configured with tags and network settings.

edges.notes: Migration team populates DynamoDB with metadata, subnets, IPs, and tag definitions.
On-premises agent sends TCP dependency and performance metrics to Application Discovery Service.
Continuous block-level data replication from on-premises server to EC2 hot replica.
CloudEndure agent controls block replication into the hot replica instance.
Migration team issues ChatOps command via Slack to trigger migration.
Slack integration calls API on the Migration Factory EC2 instance.
Migration Factory reads target parameters and metadata from DynamoDB.
Migration Factory queries Application Discovery Service for TCP and sizing metadata.
Migration Factory calls CloudEndure API to halt volume replication.
Migration Factory triggers creation of AMI from the hot replica staging storage.
Migration Factory shares the encrypted AMI to the target account.
Migration Factory launches and configures target EC2 instance in the destination account.
